claims.text: MoNbTaTiW is a refractory high-entropy alloy suitable as the substrate system considered.
MoNbTaTiW can be produced by conventional melting or additive manufacturing.
Applying a pre-formed Si-Cr-Fe-based silicide coating to MoNbTaTiW will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance relative to the uncoated alloy.
A fused-slurry deposition process can produce the proposed silicide coating on MoNbTaTiW.
The coating will have an outer high-silicon layer predominantly consisting of MSi2.
The coating will have an inner lower-silicon layer predominantly consisting of M5Si3.
The intervention will form an adherent and continuous silicide/oxide scale on the alloy surface.
At high temperature, the silicide coating will react to form a dense, stable, silica-based oxide layer.
The silica-based oxide layer will act as a diffusion barrier that slows oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy.
Slower oxygen ingress will reduce further oxidation of the underlying refractory high-entropy alloy.
Under exposure in air at about 900 degrees Celsius for 10 hours, the coated sample will have lower oxidation weight gain than the uncoated sample.
Under those conditions, the coated sample will develop a more intact and less porous oxide layer than the uncoated sample.
The expected benefit is bounded to oxidative exposure around 900 degrees Celsius in air for up to 10 hours.
Refractory high-entropy alloys generally have poor oxidation resistance that obstructs their use in high-temperature engineering applications.
Coated and uncoated MoNbTaTiW samples should be compared after static-air exposure at 900 degrees Celsius for 10 hours.
Failure to obtain at least about 20% lower oxidation weight gain together with a more continuous oxide layer in the coated samples would falsify the hypothesis.
